titre: Cochlear Implantation in a Child With Arnold-Chiari Syndrome, Severe Inner Ear Malformations, and Cochlear Nerve Hypoplasia: A Case Report.
auteurs: Skarżyński PH, Chodkiewicz A, Czajka N, Skarżyński H.
resume_source: BACKGROUND Arnold-Chiari syndrome is a congenital malformation of the posterior cranial fossa associated with neurological and otoneurological abnormalities, including hearing loss of variable severity. Cochlear implantation in patients with complex central nervous system malformations remains challenging due to uncertain auditory outcomes. This study aimed to evaluate the feasibility and early outcomes of cochlear implantation in a child with Arnold-Chiari syndrome and severe bilateral inner ear malformations. CASE REPORT A 1.5-year-old girl with Arnold-Chiari malformation, hydrocephalus, spina bifida, and profound bilateral sensorineural hearing loss was evaluated for cochlear implantation. Imaging studies revealed severe bilateral inner ear malformations, including cochlear hypoplasia, accompanied by multiple intracranial abnormalities. Despite early hearing aid use, auditory development remained limited. The patient underwent left-sided cochlear implantation with a MED-EL SYNCHRONY 2 device using a standard electrode array. Intraoperatively, significant cerebrospinal fluid leakage ("gusher") occurred during cochleostomy and was successfully controlled using autologous tissues and tissue adhesive. Twelve months after implantation, follow-up audiological evaluation demonstrated improved behavioral auditory responses and increased responsiveness to environmental sounds, as reported by the parents. CONCLUSIONS Cochlear implantation may provide meaningful auditory benefit in selected patients with Arnold-Chiari syndrome despite severe inner ear and central nervous system abn...

titre: Antifungal ototoxicity, itraconazole, and approaches to its mitigation: a review of a sparse evidence base.
auteurs: Vališ M, Juklová K, Skorunková R, Frydrych Š, Halúsková S.
resume_source: 1. introduction Hearing loss is a recognised hazard of aminoglycosides and platinum chemotherapy, but the auditory risk of antifungal drugs has received far less attention. Itraconazole lists hearing loss in its prescribing information, yet dedicated peer-reviewed auditory studies appear absent. 2. areas covered The original 139-record Web of Science (WoS) title-only corpus was retained to map the wider ototoxicity field. A targeted WoS Topic-field sensitivity search using antifungal-specific terms and broader auditory outcomes retrieved 153 records, of which 18 direct antifungal auditory safety/toxicity studies were retained. No dedicated auditory study of itraconazole was identified. The expanded evidence shows formulation- and route-dependent topical effects, a pharmacovigilance signal for oral terbinafine, no auditory brainstem response shift in a short-duration animal study of systemic voriconazole or caspofungin, and rare hearing-loss reports plus a pharmacovigilance signal for amphotericin B. Otoprotection evidence from other drug classes is considered for transferable mitigation principles. 3. expert opinion The broader search shows a heterogeneous but sparse evidence base rather than an absence of evidence. Human systemic azole data remain particularly limited, and itraconazole lacks dedicated auditory investigation. Baseline and serial audiometry, separation of drug effects from infection and interacting medicines, and mechanistic studies are priorities.

titre: Literary Element Use in Written Narratives for Third-Grade Children Who Are Deaf and Hard of Hearing.
auteurs: Grey B, Lund EA, Werfel KL.
resume_source: Purpose This study examined literary element use in third-grade written narratives to determine if children who are deaf and hard of hearing (DHH) and their peers with typical hearing (TH) met macrostructure writing proficiency expectations addressed in the Common Core State Standards. Method Participants included 134 children who completed third grade across three groups: children who used cochlear implants (CIs), children who used hearing aids (HAs), and children with TH. Given a picture prompt, participants composed a written narrative. Using the third-grade Common Core State Standards that addressed macrostructure, written narratives were scored with a rubric that outlined the criteria for meeting seven literary element categories: characters, actions, feelings, dialogue, topic, sequence, and plot. Results CI, HA, and TH children did not meet most macrostructure literary element criteria for narrative writing addressed in the third-grade Common Core State Standards. Literary element outcomes did not significantly differ between CI, HA, and TH groups, except for topic. Conclusions DHH and TH third-grade students did not demonstrate strong macrostructure writing skills in their written narratives. To build a solid writing foundation, elementary students, regardless of hearing status, would benefit from general and genre-specific writing interventions that incorporate self-regulating strategies throughout their writing process to facilitate the transition from learning to write to writing to learn. Supplemental material https://doi.org/10.23641/asha.34259406.

titre: Paired-ear tympanometric pressure patterns and hearing recovery in unilateral sudden sensorineural hearing loss: a retrospective cohort study
auteurs: Tianyu Zhang, Yaxue Xie, Yingxuan Li, Haibo Zhang, Hanzhai Tian, Ziye Zhu, Zhiyu Yang, Zhenlin Wang
resume_source: Background Sudden sensorineural hearing loss (SSNHL) remains difficult to phenotype and predict. Tympanometry is routinely performed, yet its quantitative pressure information is largely discarded once conductive hearing loss is excluded. We used a paired-ear strategy to compare middle-ear pressure between the affected and contralateral ears in unilateral SSNHL. Methods We retrospectively studied 203 adults with unilateral SSNHL and bilateral tympanometric peak pressure (TPP) measurements. Rather than relying on a single abnormality threshold, we integrated signed interaural differences, absolute pressure asymmetry, laterality-aware pressure phenotypes, and threshold-sensitivity analyses. Among patients with follow-up audiometry, hearing recovery was quantified as both continuous hearing gain and clinically meaningful ≥15-dB improvement, and was further examined in relation to categorical and continuous TPP phenotypes. Results Paired-ear analysis showed no significant pressure shift in the affected ear compared with the contralateral ear ( p = 0.410), indicating no consistent affected-ear pressure abnormality at the population level. Laterality-aware classification identified affected-ear-only negative pressure in 14 patients (6.9%) and contralateral-ear-only negative pressure in 11 patients (5.4%). This subgroup would be largely invisible using conventional single-ear classification. Across complementary binary, continuous, and multivariable analyses, tympanometric pressure showed no robust relationship with short-term hearing recovery, and this conclusion remained stable ...

titre: Speech Perception in Noise in Individuals With Tinnitus: Top-Down and Bottom-Up Processes
auteurs: Halime Sümeyra Sevmez, Emre Gürses, Hatice Merve Yücel, Meral Didem Türkyilmaz, Harvey Dillon
resume_source: Objectives: To evaluate speech-in-noise and spatial listening performance in patients with tinnitus by examining the potential contributions of top-down and bottom-up processes. Design: Thirty-one patients with tinnitus and 31 age-matched controls without tinnitus (participants with normal hearing), aged 18 to 60 years, underwent audiological evaluation. All participants completed the Listening in Spatialized Noise–Universal Test to assess speech-in-noise performance under different spatial conditions and cognitive tests (Serial Digit Learning and Stroop) to assess attention and memory. Results: Hearing thresholds did not differ significantly between groups ( p > 0.05), although a significant main effect of frequency was observed ( p < 0.001). Participants with tinnitus demonstrated poorer speech-in-noise performance than controls across both colocated and spatially separated listening conditions [ F (1,60) = 12.53, p = 0.001], whereas spatial advantage ( t = 1.08, p = 0.28) and cognitive performance (all p > 0.05) were comparable between groups. Conclusions: Patients with tinnitus demonstrated poorer speech-in-noise performance than controls in both spatially separated and colocated listening conditions. Spatial advantage and cognitive test performance were comparable between groups, suggesting that the between-group difference in speech-in-noise performance was evident across both listening conditions rather than being limited to spatial cue utilization.

titre: Longitudinal Growth of Mandated Hearing Aid Benefits in the US.

titre: Jervell and Lange-Nielsen Syndrome
auteurs: Faridi R, Przybylski R, Saenen J, Hertzano R, Newman WG, Friedman TB.
resume_source: Clinical characteristics Jervell and Lange-Nielsen syndrome (JLNS) is characterized by bilateral sensorineural hearing loss (SNHL), vestibular dysfunction, and QTc prolongation on repeated testing. Iron deficiency anemia may be present in some people with KCNQ1 pathogenic variants. The hearing loss is most often congenital and severe to profound, although milder degrees of hearing loss have been described. Temporal bone anatomy on CT is normal. Vestibular dysfunction may result in gross motor delay (including later ages of walking), balance impairment, and absent physiologic nystagmus. In the absence of other reversible conditions that prolong the QT interval, serial 12-lead surface electrocardiograms show a prolonged QTc interval using the Bazzet formula exceeding 450 ms in prepubertal children, 460 ms in adult men, and 470 ms in adult women or a high probability long QT syndrome (LQTS) score ≥3.5. Repeated QTc prolongation must be observed, as a large overlap exists between unaffected individuals and those with LQTS. In KCNQ1-JLNS1, QTc prolongation is often severe (>500 ms) and associated with high risk for ventricular arrhythmias (e.g., torsade de pointes that can spontaneously resolve or degenerate into ventricular fibrillation), which if left untreated may result in syncope or sudden cardiac death (SCD). In KCNE1-JLNS2, QTc prolongation is reported to be less severe, though significant risk for malignant ventricular arrhythmias remains. resume_source: Objectives: The Vanderbilt Classroom Listening Assessment Short Survey (VCLASS) was previously developed as a tool to monitor listening difficulties experienced by school-aged children in classrooms. However, the previous statistical approach used in the initial validation did not fully evaluate the questionnaire’s psychometric properties, did not take into account the ordinal nature of responses, and did not contrast hearing-aided versus hearing-unaided conditions. The present study aimed to evaluate the psychometric properties of the 15‑item VCLASS using item response theory (IRT) in both hearing-aided and unaided conditions. More specifically, we aimed to (1) assess the latent structure for each listening condition (unaided and aided); (2) determine appropriate IRT-based models to estimate item discrimination and threshold parameters for each listening condition; (3) assess reliability from the IRT-based model; and (4) evaluate both uniform and nonuniform age-related differential item functioning (DIF) under each listening condition. Design: We applied IRT-based analyses to analyze responses previously collected from children aged 9 to 17 years with unilateral hearing loss. All children (n = 1148) completed the VCLASS imagining they were not using a device (unaided); most children (n = 897) also completed the VCLASS imagining they were using their personal listening device (aided). titre: Task force of the Brazilian Society of Otology and the Brazilian Academy of Neurotology: Menière's Disease.
auteurs: Pauna HF, Silva VAR, Lavinsky J, de Giacomo Carneiro C, Mangia LRL, Grasel SS, de Oliveira Beck RM, Salmito MC, de Carvalho Lopes K, Mezzalira R, Furtado PL, Sampaio ALL, Mano PM, Bertoldo C, de Carvalho RCB, Joffily L, de Rezende Oliveira LN, Lamounier P, Selaimen FA, Lavinsky L, Lopes da Silva MN,...
resume_source: Objective To critically review the available evidence on the pathophysiology and diagnosis of Menière's disease and to provide consensus-based recommendations developed by a task force of the Brazilian Society of Otology and the Brazilian Academy of Neurotology. Methods A task force consisting of experts in otology and neurotology was established to review the scientific literature and develop thematic sections of the document. The content was discussed in both in-person and remote meetings until consensus was achieved. Recommendations were graded according to level of evidence and strength of recommendation using standardized systems for the evaluation of therapeutic interventions and diagnostic methods. Results Menière's disease is a heterogeneous clinical condition characterized by recurrent episodes of vertigo, fluctuating sensorineural hearing loss, tinnitus, and aural fullness. Endolymphatic hydrops represents the most consistent histopathologic finding; however, it does not alone explain the clinical expression of the disease. Current evidence indicates the involvement of multifactorial mechanisms, including genetic predisposition, immune dysfunction, inflammatory processes, and changes in inner ear ion homeostasis. Diagnosis remains primarily clinical, based on international criteria, with serial audiometry playing a key role. Electrophysiologic testing and imaging may be useful in selected situations. Clinical variability supports the concept of subphenotypes with potential diagnostic and prognostic implications. Conclusion Menière's disease should be recognized as...

titre: The Relationship among Obesity, Intracranial Hypertension, and Cerebrospinal Fluid Leak.
auteurs: Ojeda-Badillo G, Naples JG.
resume_source: Idiopathic intracranial hypertension (IIH) is a disorder characterized by elevated intracranial pressure without identifiable lesion or secondary cause. Patients can often present with otolaryngologic manifestations of IIH, such as pulsatile tinnitus, aural fullness, and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) leak. Obesity plays an important role as a risk factor for both IIH and CSF leak as similar pathophysiological processes underly both presentations. Understanding the nuanced presentation of this condition is important for the otolaryngologist who routinely evaluates patients with these symptoms and has implications for management decisions. In this article, we discuss the relationship among obesity, IIH, and CSF leak.

titre: The history of tinnitus: from ancient interpretations to contemporary neuroscience and neuromodulation.
auteurs: William R.
resume_source: Objective To review the historical evolution of tinnitus from ancient civilizations to contemporary neuromodulation-based therapies. Methods A narrative historical review was undertaken using PubMed, Google Scholar, historical archives, classical medical texts, and landmark otological publications. Sources were selected according to historical significance, relevance to tinnitus, and contribution to major shifts in its conceptualisation and management. Results As a non-systematic narrative review, this study traces the conceptual paradigm shifts in tinnitus understanding. Early civilizations attributed tinnitus to supernatural causes, while Greek and Islamic scholars introduced humoral and clinical theories. The nineteenth century established scientific otology, rooting tinnitus in peripheral ear pathology. Crucially, modern neuroscience prompted a paradigm shift from these peripheral cochlear models to central network theories. This shift has driven the exploration of specific neuromodulation modalities, such as repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) and bimodal stimulation. Conclusion The history of tinnitus reflects the broader evolution of medicine, progressing from superstition to evidence-based neuro-otological science.

titre: Effect of the vagus nerve stimulation combined with sound therapy for tinnitus treatment: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
auteurs: Rezapour M, Jalali MM, Nemati S, Borna A.
resume_source: Background Tinnitus is a prevalent hearing problem linked to anxiety and depression. It currently has no cure. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to explore the potential association of combining vagus nerve stimulation (VNS) with auditory stimulation in alleviating tinnitus, recognizing the exploratory nature of evidence. Methods Six databases were searched from 1990 to 2023 (2025 updated) for randomized clinical trials, observational studies, and case studies with at least one group receiving invasive or non-invasive VNS with sound for tinnitus management. Eligible studies used validated questionnaires to quantify tinnitus distress or severity in patients compared with controls or pre-treatment status. Two reviewers extracted participant, intervention, blinding, assessment, and outcome data. The risk of bias was assessed with ROBINS-I for non-randomized studies and ROB2 for randomized controlled trials. PRISMA guidelines were followed. Results Eight studies were included in the systematic review and six in the meta-analysis. The Tinnitus Handicap Inventory (THI) and the Visual Analogue Scale (VAS) were suitable for meta-analysis. The analysis was primarily based on within-group pre‑post changes, not between‑group comparisons. titre: Otoferlin Gene Therapy: Narrative Review for Ear and Hearing Special Issue: Gene Therapy for Hearing Loss
auteurs: Jenna Devare, Audrey P. Lawrence, John A. Germiller
resume_source: In the last decade, gene therapy has shown promise in treating many genetic disorders. Hereditary hearing impairment represents one of the next promising frontiers. Many initial development efforts have focused on hearing impairment caused by mutations in the otoferlin gene ( OTOF ), as these mutations cause profound deafness in the setting of preserved auditory outer hair cells, which often remain for many years after birth. Animal models have shown that the target cells for gene delivery, the inner hair cells, are also present and viable, and they reside in a structurally intact organ that is otherwise functional. Recent remarkable successes reported with OTOF gene therapy serve as proof of concept that gene therapy can effectively and safely improve hearing for this and likely other forms of genetic deafness. Here, the authors review the otoferlin protein and its role in hearing, the role of pathogenic variants in OTOF in hearing loss, the natural history of the condition, and the results of preclinical studies and of current human clinical trials of OTOF gene therapy.

titre: Gene Therapy: Routes of Inner Ear Delivery
auteurs: Erdem Yildiz, Christoph Arnoldner
resume_source: Abstract: Gene delivery and the various routes of administration used to deliver viral vectors constitute a rapidly evolving field, with recent success in restoring hearing in children with OTOF variants in ongoing clinical otoferlin trials. With the rise of gene therapy for major hereditary hearing disorders, both syndromic and nonsyndromic, there has been parallel progress in the development of new delivery methods. Advances in intratympanic injection of antibiotics and corticosteroids, along with nearly half a century of experience in cochlear implantation surgery, have enabled multiple local and systemic approaches to access the inner ear. Recent industry investment in gene therapy and delivery technologies has accelerated scientific progress, underscoring the need for continuous evaluation of the most suitable gene delivery strategies for different causes of hearing loss. Although most gene delivery in animal models has been performed via round window membrane injection, yielding promising results in cochlear hair cell transduction, potential drawbacks remain for clinical translation—particularly limited vector distribution, which may result in a basal-to-apical gradient. Venting procedures such as stapes footplate fenestration or canalostomy have been explored to mitigate these limitations, and recent intrathecal or even in utero injections have been investigated as alternative approaches. Hearing loss can be inherited in multiple ways, and patient treatment with gene delivery, or even the type of gene therapy itself, may vary with the recent success of CRISPR/Cas-bas...

titre: Genetics of Hearing Loss
auteurs: Sandrine Marlin, Margaux Serey-Gaut, Natalie Loundon
resume_source: Since 1995, advancements in human genetics have elucidated many of the causes of hearing loss. Currently, over 150 genes are identified as responsible for nonsyndromic sensorineural hearing loss, and more than 200 are linked to syndromic forms (for review, see Hereditary Hearing Loss Homepage, https://hereditaryhearingloss.org). Genetic epidemiology is better understood for congenital hearing loss than for progressive adult-onset forms. It is estimated that three-quarters of early-onset hearing loss has a genetic origin, the remaining causes being acquired (prenatal cytomegalovirus infection, meningitis, sound trauma, temporal bone injuries). This article is an update of the main etiologies in genetic hearing loss.

titre: Echoes of Renewal: Rebuilding the Mammalian Inner Ear
auteurs: Ippei Kishimoto, Lingjun Zhang, Tracy Z. Cheng, Alan G. Cheng
resume_source: Abstract: Hearing loss and dizziness are the most common sensory disorders worldwide. About 5% of the world’s population is affected by disabling hearing loss, and the prevalence is projected to increase over the next several decades. Cochlear hair cells are essential in converting sound vibrations into electrical signals, which are then relayed centrally via the spiral ganglion neurons and lead to sound perception. The irreversible loss of cochlear hair cells is the most common pathology underlying sensorineural hearing loss in humans. In stark contrast, nonmammalian species such as chicken and zebrafish spontaneously regenerate hair cells from endogenous supporting cells after hair cell damage, and the mechanisms of this process are starting to be revealed. Advances in the understanding of inner ear hair cell development have led to novel protocols to efficiently generate mouse and human inner ear organoids. Several new and promising reprogramming approaches have recently been established to induce hair cell regeneration in the mature mouse cochlear and vestibular organs. In this review, we will discuss these recent advances, the implications for treatments for human hearing loss and balance dysfunction, and future directions of the field.

titre: Advances in Stem Cell Therapy for Hearing Loss
auteurs: Pavan S. Krishnan, Diane Jung, Julia A. Morris, Pei-Ciao Tang, Xue Z. Liu
resume_source: Abstract: Hearing loss is the most common sensory disorder, causing substantial impacts on language development, literacy, mood, and cognition. Sensorineural hearing loss, caused by injury to the cochlear hair cells, cochlear nerve, or central auditory pathways, accounts for most cases of hearing loss. Existing therapies for sensorineural hearing loss include hearing aids and cochlear implants; however, these modalities have limited efficacy in noisy environments, variable hearing outcomes, and limited frequency discrimination. There are currently no Food and Drug Administration-approved cellular, molecular, or pharmacological therapies available. Stem cell therapy is an emerging and promising approach to treating sensorineural hearing loss through transplanting exogenous stem cells into the cochlea. Stem cell-based inner ear systems have been crucial to studying how stem cells can mimic or restore the function of the inner ear. The two-dimensional culture system has been instrumental in understanding pluripotent stem cell differentiation in the inner ear neuroepithelium. However, they are unable to mimic tissue-specific architecture and specific cellular interactions. Researchers subsequently moved to develop differentiation protocols in three-dimensional inner ear organoids, which more closely resemble in vivo structures. Such approaches are a promising step forward in the development of stem cell therapies focusing on structures in the cochlea that have limited to no ability to regenerate, including hair cells, spiral ganglion neurons, and spiral ligament fibrocytes. Fut...

titre: Emerging Therapies for Genetic Deafness: The Rise of Precision Gene Editing
auteurs: Ghizlene Lahlou, Maxence Cornille, Nicolas Lai, Marie-José Lecomte, Saaid Safieddine
resume_source: Hearing loss is a prevalent sensory disorder with profound social and health impacts. Although hearing aids and cochlear implants can significantly restore auditory perception, they do not address the underlying genetic causes. Inherited forms of hearing loss, often monogenic, are ideal candidates for gene therapy, particularly since over 150 genes have been linked to deafness. Advances in vector engineering and genome editing technologies now enable precise targeting of auditory cells within the inner ear. Technologies such as Clustered Regularly Interspaced Short Palindromic Repeats-Cas systems, base editing, and prime editing offer powerful tools to correct pathogenic variants at their native genomic loci. This review summarizes the current landscape of gene editing approaches for both hereditary and acquired hearing loss, emphasizing key preclinical studies in mouse models encompassing dominant and recessive forms of deafness. We discuss the advantages and limitations of different editing techniques, vector delivery systems, and administration routes, and explore obstacles including editing efficiency, cell-specific targeting, and the translation of these therapies to humans. Collectively, these advances represent a pivotal step toward variant-specific, durable, and potentially curative treatments for hearing loss.

titre: Consumer preferences for hearing health care information and services as described by older adults surveyed in Australia, Canada, England, and the United States.
auteurs: Alnafjan F, Davis AC, Lee ML, McMahon CM, Mokdad AH, Mosley CL, Pichora-Fuller MK, Tremblay KL.
resume_source: Background Age-related hearing loss is a global public health concern and yet hearing health care (HHC) services remain underutilized. Understanding the HHC experiences of older adults is essential to addressing why existing systems are underutilized. Therefore, we surveyed older adults to determine their preferences for HHC service delivery. In this cross-sectional survey study, we report where they preferred to obtain HHC information, undergo hearing tests, and acquire hearing devices. We also examined whether these preferences varied by degree of hearing loss, help-seeking experience, survey mode (online or in person), age, or country. Methods Using survey questions that were co-created with consumers, responses were collected online and in person prior to the pandemic (2016-2018) in the United States (USA), Canada (CAN), Australia (AUS), and England (EN). Third-party firms recruited convenience samples from each region. Participants, aged 60 + and proficient in English, responded to three questions: "Where would you prefer to get information about HHC?" (8,151 respondents, 14 response options), "Where would you most like to get your hearing tested?" (8,035 respondents, 8 options), and "From which of the following places would you MOST like to get hearing aids (or other types of hearing devices) if you needed them?" (8,151 respondents, 11 options). Participants could select multiple options. Hearing thresholds were obtained from in-person respondents and used to impute hearing loss estimates for online respondents. Results Across all questions, respondents consistently p...

titre: [Chances and challenges in the prevention and treatment of early childhood hearing loss: the AWMF guideline on congenital CMV infection].
auteurs: Kummer P, Buxmann H, Roll C, Enders M, Goelz R, Modrow S, Leitlinien-Gruppe S2k Leitlinie „Zytomegalievirus-Infektion (CMV)“.
resume_source: After genetic causes, congenital cytomegalovirus (cCMV) infection is the leading infectious cause of congenital and early childhood hearing loss. The 2025 German S2k guideline on prevention, diagnosis, and treatment of CMV infection in pregnant women and congenital CMV infection in neonates and children published by the Association of the Scientific Medical Societies in Germany (Arbeitsgemeinschaft der Wissenschaftlichen Medizinischen Fachgesellschaften, AWMF; 093-003 [24]) provides corresponding recommendations and summarizes the current evidence. Hygiene counseling of pregnant women, targeted diagnostic testing during pregnancy and in neonates, and antiviral therapeutic options are important measures for prevention and treatment of congenital CMV infection. Universal newborn hearing screening (UNHS) is decisive for the diagnosis of congenital hearing loss. If abnormal results are revealed in the initial and follow-up testing, polymerase chain reaction (PCR) analysis of CMV DNA in urine (gold standard) or saliva should be performed immediately-as it should be in the case of other symptoms-preferably in the maternity or pediatric hospital and certainly not later than in the second to third week of life. In the case of symptomatic congenital CMV infection, causal treatment of congenital hearing loss can be offered as early as during the first 30 days of life-both for clinically symptomatic infants and for those with isolated hearing loss. Treatment may reduce the severity of hearing loss, stabilize hearing, or prevent progression. Long-term aftercare is essential to recogniz...

titre: Ear-Worn Inertial Measurement of Sit-to-Stand and Sit-to-Walk Movements: Algorithm Development and Validation.
auteurs: Fawden T, Edwards A, Roberts IV, Dunne H, Stone T, Bance M.
resume_source: Background Sit-to-stand and sit-to-walk are common functional movements that provide insight into an individual's functional mobility. Developing comprehensive measures of these movements using ear-worn inertial measurement units (IMUs), which are increasingly incorporated into widely used devices such as hearing aids and headphones, could provide a means of monitoring older adults and individuals with movement disorders with minimal additional burden. Objective This paper aimed to introduce comprehensive outcome measures for sit-to-stand and sit-to-walk movements based on data from ear-worn IMUs, and to evaluate their agreement with an optical motion capture reference. Methods Data were analyzed from 62 participants, of whom 46 (18 male and 28 female; median age 27, IQR 15 years) did not have a known underlying movement condition and 16 (7 male and 9 female; median age 62, IQR 23 years) did. The participants wore a bespoke 3D-printed headset that contained 6-axis IMUs placed beside their left and right ears. A reflective marker was placed on each participant's seventh cervical vertebra to provide an optical motion capture reference. Each participant performed 3 sit-to-stand movements and 3 sit-to-walk movements. The reported outcome metrics included overall and subphase durations, acceleration, velocity, power, movement smoothness, and hesitation. Agreement between ear-derived and optical outcomes was evaluated using linear mixed-effects analyses accounting for repeated trials within participants, including systematic and proportional bias, limits of agreement, root mean s...

titre: Cochlear Implant Training in Doctor of Audiology Programs: A Survey Study.
auteurs: Hall M, Windmill I, Sprouse B, Zwolan T.
resume_source: Purpose As the population of cochlear implant (CI) candidates and recipients grows, there is a need for more audiologists to meet their clinical needs. Little information exists regarding the perception of recent doctorate of audiology (AuD) graduates and the training they received related to CI. Method We surveyed audiologists who graduated from an accredited AuD program between 2017 and 2023 and asked them several questions about their level of satisfaction regarding their AuD studies. The survey included questions about current work setting, areas of rotation available, and instructor characteristics related to areas in the AuD. Results Respondents demonstrated high levels of satisfaction with their AuD training overall; 93% reported they were "very" or "somewhat" satisfied. Sixty-three percent reported they were "completely" or "somewhat satisfied" with the training related to CI. Most dissatisfied respondents reported that this was due to limited opportunities for hands-on work with the CI population. Seventy-two percent indicated they were "very" or "somewhat satisfied" with their CI instructor, and many tended to report higher satisfaction when instructors were clinicians with practical experience. CI rotations with adults were more prevalent than pediatric CI placements, and both were rated as less available than pediatric and adult hearing aids and diagnostic testing. A significant number of recent graduates reported gaps in their learning of topics related to insurance, reimbursement, billing, and coding. titre: Cochlear Implant Referrals in Adults With Severe-to-Profound Hearing Loss in the United Kingdom (CIRCA-2): Protocol for a Repeat National Multicenter Retrospective Observational Study.
auteurs: North AS, Swords C, Checkland P, Daniels J, Denton OG, Habeeb A, Lim KH, Jarratt-Barnham I, Rajgor A, Tailor BV, Wong J, Muzaffar J.
resume_source: Background Cochlear implantation (CI) is a highly effective intervention for adults with severe-to-profound hearing loss, yet uptake across the United Kingdom remains low despite clear National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE 2019) guidance and well-established clinical benefits. The original Cochlear Implant Referral Criteria Audit (CIRCA-1) identified marked inequities in access to CIs in 2022, with lower referral rates among older adults, males, and individuals from socioeconomically deprived areas, alongside individuals from minority ethnic backgrounds being less likely to be informed of their eligibility for referral. Since then, national awareness initiatives and the expansion of the existing local "CI Champions" scheme have aimed to address these inequities, improve awareness of CI candidacy, and improve the quality of discussions with patients about options for CI referral. This repeat assessment aims to assess the success of these interventions to identify improvements in access to CIs as well as persisting barriers. Objective CIRCA-2 is a national, multicenter, retrospective observational audit designed to re-evaluate adult CI referral pathways and measure progress since the first audit cycle. Methods The study will include adults assessed in secondary-care ear, nose, throat, and audiology departments between July and December 2025 whose audiometric thresholds meet NICE TA566 criteria. Participating centers will identify eligible patients using the British Cochlear Implant Group Crystal Report within Auditbase, and anonymized demographic, audiometri...

titre: Determinants of auditory performance after cochlear implantation in post-lingual adults: beyond the duration of hearing loss.
auteurs: Caride M, Almeida J.
resume_source: Purpose Prolonged auditory deprivation progressively compromises central auditory pathway integrity, yet its prognostic impact in post-lingual adults undergoing cochlear implantation remains poorly defined. This study evaluates the influence of hearing loss duration - expressed in absolute terms, dichotomised by the conventional 10-year threshold, and as a proportion of lifetime with hearing loss - on auditory performance, and identifies the clinical determinants associated with the immediate activation effect and the post-implantation trajectory. Methods Single-centre, retrospective, observational study at Unidade Local de Saúde de Santo António, including 109 post-lingual adults undergoing CI between 2018 and 2024, with a minimum follow-up of 12 months. Auditory performance was assessed through pure-tone average, speech reception threshold, and speech discrimination score. Longitudinal modelling used linear mixed-effects models, distinguishing the immediate activation effect from subsequent temporal progression. Results Patients with longer hearing loss duration presented greater pre-implantation auditory impairment across all metrics, following a continuous dose-response relationship with no evidence of a threshold effect. The 10-year criterion showed no discriminative value - either in the immediate effect or in the post-implantation trajectory, which was equivalent between groups. Ear selection for implantation and pre-operative hearing aid status were the strongest determinants of the level reached at activation. The proportion of hearing loss duration covered by hear...

titre: Evaluating the Effectiveness of Over-the-Counter Hearing Aids in Ageing Populations With Hearing Loss.
auteurs: Kim GY, Jo M, Cho YS, Lee S, Moon IJ.
resume_source: Background and objectives Hearing loss (HL) is common among older adults and associated with adverse health outcomes. Although hearing aids (HAs) are effective for mild to moderately severe HL, their use is limited by cost and stigma. To improve accessibility, the U.S. Food and Drug Administration has authorized over-the-counter (OTC) HAs. This study compared the performance of OTC HAs with that of prescription HAs in older adults with mild-to-moderate HL. Subjects and methods In this prospective cohort study, 30 older adults were evaluated using six HA models: one prescription HA (ReSound ONE) and five OTC HAs (Lexie B2, Vibe Air, Vibe Nano8, Jabra Enhance Plus, and Olive Smart Ear Plus). The effectiveness was assessed using sound field audiometry, word recognition scores (WRS), speech perception in noise (SPIN), and real-ear measurements (REMs). Repeated-measures analysis of variance was used for the analysis. Results Significant primary effects of the auditory test (p Conclusions OTC HAs demonstrated a performance comparable to that of prescription HAs and may serve as a cost-effective option for older adults with mild-to-moderate HL.
